The earlier pages of this track price one contract at a time. A reinsurer does
not hold one contract. Larkspur Re holds five, on three cedents, and the same
windstorm can hit all of them in the same year. This page adds the five
contracts into one book, measures the book's tail, splits the book's capital
back to the contracts, and asks which contracts earn their keep.

This is the R twin of the Python guide
[`cat-7-portfolio.md`](cat-7-portfolio.md): the same sections, the same files
and the same numbers. Each R chunk is followed by the text it prints, and
`R/prospicio/tests/test-guides.R` requires each one to print exactly that text.

The story, the files and the notation are on
[the overview](cat-0-overview.qmd). Nothing here is typed in by hand: every
attachment, limit and share comes from `cat_book_contracts.csv`.

## 1. The idea

Each row of the year event loss table belongs to one simulated year, and every
contract sees the same 2,000 years. So the book's loss in a year is the sum of
the five contracts' losses in that year. No copula and no reordering are
needed for the dependence that the events carry: one event in the catalog
lands on several cedents at once. That is the only dependence in this book,
though. The script that wrote it draws each cedent's loss from an event
independently, so the correlated part of secondary uncertainty (page 1) is
not correlated across cedents here. A real model that shares it would give
the book a heavier tail than this page shows.

Three questions follow from that sum.

- **How bad is the book's bad year?** A tail measure of the summed loss, here
  TVaR at 99%: the mean of the worst 1% of years.
- **Who is responsible for it?** A split of the book's TVaR back to the
  contracts. The Euler split gives each contract its mean loss in the years
  that make the book's tail; [price allocation](pir-price-allocation.qmd)
  compares it with the other ways to split.
- **Does each contract pay for the capital it uses?** A price or a return on
  that allocated capital, set against the premium the contract actually
  charges.

## 2. The book

The chunk below repeats the reader helpers of the earlier pages (each guide
runs on its own), builds each contract's tower on its own subject loss, and
wraps each result in a `deal_run_from_tower()`. A `deal_book()` lines the runs
up year by year.

```{r}
library(prospicio)

# The data files, found from the repository root (CI) or from docs/guides (Quarto).
find_data <- function(name, dir = getwd()) {
  repeat {
    path <- file.path(dir, "examples", "data", name)
    if (file.exists(path)) return(path)
    parent <- dirname(dir)
    if (identical(parent, dir)) stop("examples/data/", name, " not found", call. = FALSE)
    dir <- parent
  }
}

read_text <- function(name) read.csv(find_data(name), colClasses = "character")
YELT <- read_text("cat_book_yelt.csv")
CONTRACTS <- read_text("cat_book_contracts.csv")
CEDENTS <- read_text("cat_book_cedents.csv")
N_YEARS <- 2000

# One cedent's years of losses, with times (fraction of the year) and peril labels.
cedent_events <- function(cedent, perils = "all") {
  rows <- YELT[YELT$cedent == cedent, ]
  if (perils != "all") rows <- rows[rows$peril %in% strsplit(perils, "+", fixed = TRUE)[[1]], ]
  year <- factor(as.integer(rows$year), levels = seq_len(N_YEARS))
  time <- ((as.integer(rows$day) - 1) * 24 + as.integer(rows$hour)) / 8760
  ev <- events_from_years(unname(split(as.double(rows$loss), year)),
                          times = unname(split(time, year)))
  with_labels(ev, list(peril = rows$peril[order(year)]))
}

num <- function(x, default = NULL) if (x != "") as.double(x) else default

# The contract's terms from cat_book_contracts.csv as a layer.
contract_layer <- function(c) {
  share <- num(c$share)
  if (c$kind == "occurrence_xl") {
    limit <- num(c$limit)
    return(xol_layer(c$contract, limit, num(c$attachment), share = share,
                     premium = num(c$rate_on_line) * limit * share,
                     reinstatement_rates = rep(num(c$reinstatement_rate),
                                               as.integer(c$reinstatements))))
  }
  if (c$kind == "aggregate_xl") {
    agg_limit <- num(c$aggregate_limit)
    return(xol_layer(c$contract, Inf, 0, share = share,
                     aggregate_deductible = num(c$aggregate_deductible),
                     aggregate_limit = agg_limit,
                     premium = num(c$rate_on_line) * agg_limit * share))
  }
  premium <- share * as.double(CEDENTS$cat_premium[CEDENTS$cedent == c$cedent])
  with_ceding_commission(
    xol_layer(c$contract, num(c$limit), 0, share = share,
              aggregate_limit = num(c$aggregate_limit), premium = premium),
    num(c$ceding_commission))
}

# The contract's subject loss: its cedent and perils, grouped by its hours clause.
subject <- function(c) {
  e <- cedent_events(c$cedent, c$perils)
  if (c$hours != "") hours_clause(e, as.double(c$hours)) else e
}

deals <- CONTRACTS$contract
towers <- list()
results <- list()
for (i in seq_len(nrow(CONTRACTS))) {
  c <- CONTRACTS[i, ]
  towers[[c$contract]] <- reinsurance_tower(list(contract_layer(c)))
  results[[c$contract]] <- apply_tower(towers[[c$contract]], subject(c))
}
runs <- lapply(deals, function(d) deal_run_from_tower(d, towers[[d]], results[[d]], d))
book <- deal_book(runs)
amounts <- book_amounts(book)
cat(sprintf("%d deals, %d years\n", length(runs), as.integer(amounts@n_sims)))
cat("items:", paste(unique(amounts@keys$item), collapse = ", "), "\n")
```

```text
5 deals, 2000 years
items: premium, loss, ceding_commission, total_deductions, nmbf, margin
```

`book_summary()` gives the mean of every item by deal and for the book, with
its ratio to the mean premium. The margin here is premium less loss less the
deductions (only `corran_qs` has one, its ceding commission). Larkspur's own
expenses are not in the data, so the margin is before them.

```{r}
s <- book_summary(book)
item_mean <- function(s, d, i) s$mean[s$deal == d & s$item == i]
item_ratio <- function(s, d, i) s$ratio[s$deal == d & s$item == i]
cat(sprintf("%-12s%9s%8s%8s%8s%7s\n", "deal", "premium", "loss", "deduct", "margin", "LR"))
for (d in c(deals, "total")) {
  cat(sprintf("%-12s%9.3f%8.3f%8.3f%8.3f%7.3f\n", d, item_mean(s, d, "premium"),
              item_mean(s, d, "loss"), item_mean(s, d, "total_deductions") + 0,
              item_mean(s, d, "margin"), item_ratio(s, d, "loss")))
}
```

```text
deal          premium    loss  deduct  margin     LR
alder_cat_1     1.800   0.823   0.000   0.977  0.457
alder_cat_2     1.000   0.416   0.000   0.584  0.416
bracken_cat     1.750   0.685   0.000   1.065  0.391
bracken_agg     0.450   0.162   0.000   0.288  0.360
corran_qs       3.000   1.202   0.750   1.048  0.401
total           8.000   3.289   0.750   3.961  0.411
```

## 3. Reinstatement premium is not in the book

`deal_run_from_tower()` takes a layer's deposit premium. The reinstatement
premium that the tower computes for the two Alder layers and `bracken_cat`
stays behind: `alder_cat_1`'s premium is the same 1.8 in every year, although
a year that reaches the layer pays more (#595).

Until then, build those runs by hand from the tower's result: premium in year
`j` is the deposit plus that year's reinstatement premium. Losses do not
change, so the capital below does not change either. Only the premium and the
margin do.

```{r}
deposit <- marginal(amounts, c("premium", "alder_cat_1"))@draws
cat(sprintf("alder_cat_1 book premium: min %.3f, max %.3f\n", min(deposit), max(deposit)))

# The deal's run with each year's reinstatement premium added to its deposit.
with_reinstatement_premium <- function(name) {
  by_kind <- aggregate(results[[name]], keep = c("kind", "layer"))
  rip <- marginal(by_kind, c("reinstatement_premium", name))
  if (is.null(rip)) return(deal_run_from_tower(name, towers[[name]], results[[name]], name))
  loss <- marginal(by_kind, c("ceded", name))@draws
  c <- CONTRACTS[CONTRACTS$contract == name, ]
  deal_run(name, contract_layer(c)@premium + rip@draws, loss)
}

book_rip <- deal_book(lapply(deals, with_reinstatement_premium))
s_rip <- book_summary(book_rip)
for (d in deals) {
  added <- item_mean(s_rip, d, "premium") - item_mean(s, d, "premium")
  cat(sprintf("%-12s reinstatement premium %.4f\n", d, added))
}
```

```text
alder_cat_1 book premium: min 1.800, max 1.800
alder_cat_1  reinstatement premium 0.1207
alder_cat_2  reinstatement premium 0.0203
bracken_cat  reinstatement premium 0.0959
bracken_agg  reinstatement premium 0.0000
corran_qs    reinstatement premium 0.0000
```

## 4. The book's tail

`book_distribution(book, "loss", ...)` gives three views of each deal at once.

- `total`: the book's own statistics.
- `contribution`: the deal's mean loss in the years that make the book's
  statistic. For TVaR this is the Euler split, and the contributions add up to
  the book's TVaR.
- `marginal`: the book's statistic less the same statistic of the book
  without that deal. It answers "what would we save by not writing this?".

The stand-alone TVaR of each deal comes from `capital_allocation()` below.
Here it is the first column, for comparison.

```{r}
dist <- book_distribution(book, "loss", 99, tvar_levels = 99)
loss <- select_components(select_components(amounts, "item", "loss"), "deal", deals)
alloc <- capital_allocation(loss, distortion("tvar", 0.99))
cat(sprintf("book: mean %.3f, VaR 99 %.3f, TVaR 99 %.3f\n", dist$total[["Mean"]],
            dist$total[["Percentile 99"]], dist$total[["TVaR 99"]]))
cat(sprintf("%-12s%8s%9s%10s\n", "deal", "alone", "contrib", "marginal"))
for (k in seq_along(deals)) {
  d <- deals[k]
  cat(sprintf("%-12s%8.3f%9.3f%10.3f\n", d, alloc$by_component$standalone[k],
              dist$contribution["TVaR 99", d], dist$marginal["TVaR 99", d]))
}
cat(sprintf("sum of contributions %.3f\n", sum(dist$contribution["TVaR 99", deals])))
```

```text
book: mean 3.289, VaR 99 46.505, TVaR 99 55.096
deal           alone  contrib  marginal
alder_cat_1   13.843   13.195    12.728
alder_cat_2   20.998   19.026    14.560
bracken_cat   14.136    9.397     8.840
bracken_agg    7.500    0.262     0.193
corran_qs     16.363   13.216    12.609
sum of contributions 55.096
```

Read the table one row at a time.

- `alder_cat_2` is the high Alder layer. On its own its TVaR is the largest of
  the five, and it keeps most of that in the book, because the years that
  exhaust it are the big coastal windstorms that drive the whole book.
- `bracken_agg` looks risky alone: in its worst 1% of years it pays its whole
  share of the aggregate limit. Those are mostly years of one large flood or
  storm outbreak on the plains (page 3, section 5), not the book's worst
  years, so it adds little to the book's tail.
- Contributions add up to the book's TVaR. Marginals do not: removing one deal
  changes which years are the worst, so the marginals add up to less.

## 5. A trap: the total row

`book_amounts()` holds every item for each deal *and* a `"total"` deal. A
selection on the item alone keeps that total, and `capital_allocation()` then
adds it to the deals as if it were a sixth contract. The book's TVaR doubles.

```{r}
wrong <- capital_allocation(select_components(amounts, "item", "loss"), distortion("tvar", 0.99))
right <- capital_allocation(loss, distortion("tvar", 0.99))
cat(sprintf("item only: total %.3f, components %d\n", wrong$total, nrow(wrong$by_component)))
cat(sprintf("item and deals: total %.3f, components %d\n", right$total,
            nrow(right$by_component)))
```

```text
item only: total 110.192, components 6
item and deals: total 55.096, components 5
```

Select the deals by name, `select_components(..., "deal", deals)`, every time.

## 6. Capital and diversification

`capital_allocation(loss, distortion("tvar", 0.99))` allocates the book's TVaR
by Euler, so the allocated amounts are the contributions above.
Diversification is the sum of the stand-alone TVaRs less the book's TVaR:

```
diversification = sum over deals i of TVaR(X_i) - TVaR(X_1 + ... + X_5)
```

TVaR is subadditive, so this is never negative.

```{r}
bc <- alloc$by_component
cat(sprintf("%-12s%8s%11s%8s\n", "deal", "alone", "allocated", "saved"))
for (k in seq_along(deals)) {
  cat(sprintf("%-12s%8.3f%11.3f%8.3f\n", deals[k], bc$standalone[k], bc$allocated[k],
              bc$diversification[k]))
}
cat(sprintf("sum alone %.3f, book %.3f, benefit %.3f\n", sum(bc$standalone), alloc$total,
            alloc$diversification_benefit))
```

```text
deal           alone  allocated   saved
alder_cat_1   13.843     13.195   0.648
alder_cat_2   20.998     19.026   1.973
bracken_cat   14.136      9.397   4.738
bracken_agg    7.500      0.262   7.238
corran_qs     16.363     13.216   3.147
sum alone 72.840, book 55.096, benefit 17.744
```

## 7. The book priced on its capital

`price_portfolio()` prices the book as page 6, section 2 prices one contract,
`P = (EL + r A) / (1 + r)`, with the assets `A` now the book's TVaR. It then
splits that premium to the deals by the same Euler weights
([portfolio pricing](pir-portfolio-pricing.qmd) has the theory), and prices
each deal alone as well. The premium to compare with is what Larkspur keeps:
the premium charged, plus the expected reinstatement premium of section 3,
less the deductions (Corran's ceding commission).

```{r}
pp <- price_portfolio(loss, distortion("tvar", 0.99), cost_of_capital = 0.10)
cat(sprintf("book: EL %.3f, premium %.3f, capital %.3f\n", pp$total$expected_loss,
            pp$total$premium, pp$total$capital))
kept <- function(d) item_mean(s_rip, d, "premium") - item_mean(s_rip, d, "total_deductions")
cat(sprintf("%-12s%9s%8s%9s%8s\n", "deal", "charged", "kept", "in book", "alone"))
for (k in seq_along(deals)) {
  cat(sprintf("%-12s%9.3f%8.3f%9.3f%8.3f\n", deals[k], item_mean(s, deals[k], "premium"), kept(deals[k]),
              pp$by_component$premium[k], pp$by_component$standalone_premium[k]))
}
cat(sprintf("%-12s%9.3f%8.3f%9.3f\n", "book", item_mean(s, "total", "premium"), kept("total"),
            pp$total$premium))
cat(sprintf("premium saved by diversification %.3f\n", pp$diversification))
```

```text
book: EL 3.289, premium 7.998, capital 47.097
deal          charged    kept  in book   alone
alder_cat_1     1.800   1.921    1.948   2.007
alder_cat_2     1.000   1.020    2.108   2.287
bracken_cat     1.750   1.846    1.477   1.908
bracken_agg     0.450   0.450    0.171   0.829
corran_qs       3.000   2.250    2.295   2.581
book            8.000   7.487    7.998
premium saved by diversification 1.613
```

Stand-alone, `alder_cat_1` needs the 2.007 of page 6. In the book it needs
less. The book charges 8.000, which looks like the 7.998 that a 10% return on
TVaR capital asks for, but it keeps less: 7.487 after the reinstatement
premium comes in and Corran's ceding commission goes out. So the book as a
whole falls short of the target, which section 9 confirms as a 9.0% return.
Both Alder layers keep less than their share, `alder_cat_2` about half of it.
The two Bracken contracts keep more than theirs. Corran's quota share charges
3.000 but keeps 2.250, a little under its 2.295.

## 8. The marginal price of a new contract

The allocated price shares the book's price among deals already written. A
new contract is a different question: what must it charge so that the book's
return does not fall? Take the extra assets `dA` it needs (its marginal TVaR,
the book with it less the book without it) and its expected loss `EL`. With
the same convention as above:

```
P = EL + r * (dA - P),   so   P = (EL + r * dA) / (1 + r)
```

Below, each deal is treated in turn as the last one written. The library has
no call for this, so it is done by hand from `marginal` (#588).

```{r}
r <- 0.10
cat(sprintf("%-12s%7s%8s%12s%9s\n", "deal", "EL", "dA", "marginal P", "charged"))
for (d in deals) {
  el <- dist$marginal["Mean", d]
  da <- dist$marginal["TVaR 99", d]
  p <- (el + r * da) / (1 + r)
  cat(sprintf("%-12s%7.3f%8.3f%12.3f%9.3f\n", d, el, da, p, item_mean(s, d, "premium")))
}
```

```text
deal             EL      dA  marginal P  charged
alder_cat_1   0.823  12.728       1.905    1.800
alder_cat_2   0.416  14.560       1.702    1.000
bracken_cat   0.685   8.840       1.426    1.750
bracken_agg   0.162   0.193       0.165    0.450
corran_qs     1.202  12.609       2.239    3.000
```

The marginal price is lower than the allocated price for every deal, because
each deal's marginal TVaR is at most its Euler contribution: TVaR is
subadditive, so adding a deal to a book raises the book's TVaR by no more than
the deal's share of the new book's tail. Price the next contract on its
marginal and the book's TVaR return holds. Price every contract on its
marginal and the book falls short.

## 9. A return on allocated capital

A risk-adjusted return on capital (RAROC) sets each deal's margin against the
capital allocated to it. Here capital is allocated assets less the deal's premium, as above, and the
margin includes the reinstatement premium from the hand-built runs. There is
no expense line, so this is a return before Larkspur's own costs. The library
has no output for this (#589).

```{r}
cat(sprintf("%-12s%8s%9s%8s\n", "deal", "margin", "capital", "return"))
for (k in seq_along(deals)) {
  d <- deals[k]
  a <- bc$allocated[k]
  margin <- item_mean(s_rip, d, "margin")
  premium <- item_mean(s_rip, d, "premium")
  ret <- if (a > premium) sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * margin / (a - premium)) else "none"
  cat(sprintf("%-12s%8.3f%9.3f%8s\n", d, margin, a - premium, ret))
}
margin <- item_mean(s_rip, "total", "margin")
premium <- item_mean(s_rip, "total", "premium")
cat(sprintf("%-12s%8.3f%9.3f%8s\n", "book", margin, alloc$total - premium,
            sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * margin / (alloc$total - premium))))
```

```text
deal          margin  capital  return
alder_cat_1    1.098   11.274    9.7%
alder_cat_2    0.604   18.005    3.4%
bracken_cat    1.161    7.552   15.4%
bracken_agg    0.288   -0.188    none
corran_qs      1.048   10.216   10.3%
book           4.198   46.859    9.0%
```

Against a 10% target, `alder_cat_2` is the weak contract: it uses more than a
third of the book's capital and returns a few percent on it. `bracken_agg` has
no return to show. Its premium is larger than the assets allocated to it, so
in this book it needs no shareholder capital at all, and a ratio over a
negative capital means nothing.

## 10. Reproducibility

The book's VaR above is the default inverted-cdf quantile; page 2, section 2
compares it with the other conventions, and the `k`-th largest year has no
switch yet (#582).

Every number on this page follows from four committed files and one seed.

- `examples/data/make_cat_book.py` writes the files with a fixed seed, and a
  test checks that the committed files are what it writes.
- No step on this page draws a random number: the book adds the same 2,000
  years for every contract.
- `read_ylt()` stamps the event set with a hash of the file it read, so a
  result can be traced to its input. The rebuild by `cedent_events()` drops
  that hash, so record it from `read_ylt()` once.

```{r}
ylt <- read_ylt(find_data("cat_book_yelt.csv"), year = "year", loss = "loss", slot = "slot",
                labels = c("peril", "region", "cedent"))
cat(strsplit(ylt@input_hash, ":", fixed = TRUE)[[1]][1], ylt@n_sims, "\n")
```

```text
blake3 2000
```

The hash itself is not printed here: it depends on the file's bytes, and a
checkout that turns line endings into CRLF gives a different one.

## What is missing

- reinstatement premium in `deal_run_from_tower()` (#595)
- the marginal price of a new contract in one call (#588)
- a deal's and the book's return on allocated or marginal capital
  (#589)
- in R only, a deal book's names, number of years and items, as Python's
  `DealBook.names`, `n_sims` and `items`; this page reads them from the
  contracts table and `book_amounts()` (#596)
